findings.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the raw attribute; with order_by="-datetime" the value is a datetime, so build_cursor raises TypeError and superuser/global-access callers sending optimized_pagination=true get a 500 on the first non-empty page (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840)

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, so BasePaginator.build_queryset filters datetime__lte=<int> against a datetime column and every page after the first fails; the paginator lacks the timestamp/millisecond/tolerance handling DateTimePaginator provides and cannot work on this endpoint (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843)

The negative-offset branch does queryset[negative:stop], but Django QuerySet rejects negative slice bounds with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), so a cursor like 0:-5:0 causes an unhandled 500; the comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is false, and the same failure exists in BasePaginator.get_result at line 182 for is_prev cursors with negative offset (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:872)

organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated on every request rather than only when the flag is set; organization_context.member is None for non-member callers (integration or sentry-app tokens with org:read), so those callers now get an AttributeError regardless of query params, regressing the existing endpoint (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71)

Gating uses request.user.is_superuser instead of is_active_superuser(request), violating Sentry's convention of requiring an active superuser session for privileged paths; the feature is a privileged user-toggleable path advertising access to data beyond normal pagination bounds with no legitimate reason for pagination to grant superusers different data (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71)

The change to BasePaginator.get_result affects every cursor-paginated endpoint in Sentry; a malformed forward cursor with a negative offset is now silently clamped to page 1 instead of surfacing an error, hiding client bugs and changing behavior for unrelated endpoints without justification (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182)

OptimizedCursorPaginator does not change the query at all; get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with the same build_queryset, slice, and count_hits path, so the claimed performance gains cannot be delivered and the duplication must be kept in sync with the base class (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820)

No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator, the modified BasePaginator.get_result slice logic, or the new optimized_pagination endpoint branch; a single test with one audit-log row would have caught the datetime TypeError and negative-slice failures (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820)

The added comment in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 claims negative offsets are now supported, but the line below is unchanged and nothing validates or handles them; the OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring's claim of backward compatibility with existing cursor implementations is also false since its cursor values are incompatible with DateTimePaginator cursors on the same endpoint

optimized_pagination is a new public query parameter not added to the endpoint's extend_schema parameters or documented anywhere, and it bypasses the existing query-param serializer (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:67)

Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value, so BasePaginator.build_queryset filters datetime__lte=<int> against a datetime column and every page after the first fails; the paginator lacks the timestamp/millisecond/tolerance handling DateTimePaginator provides and cannot work on this endpoint (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843)

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.get`, the new path calls `self.paginate(... paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator, order_by="-datetime")`, so the paginator key will be the model's `datetime` field. But `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` and casts to `int`, which will fail for a Django `DateTimeField` value (a `datetime` object is not valid input to `math.floor/ceil`). This makes the optimized paginator unusable on this endpoint. Additionally, `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value with no datetime parsing/normalization like `DateTimePaginator` would provide, reinforcing the mismatch for a datetime-keyed queryset.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated on every request rather than only when the flag is set; organization_context.member is None for non-member callers (integration or sentry-app tokens with org:read), so those callers now get an AttributeError regardless of query params, regressing the existing endpoint (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71)

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, `enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally as `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access`. This dereferences `organization_context.member` on every request, even when `optimized_pagination` is not set. The diff adds no None-guard, so if `organization_context.member` can be `None` for some auth paths, this would raise `AttributeError` and regress the endpoint regardless of query params.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gating uses request.user.is_superuser instead of is_active_superuser(request), violating Sentry's convention of requiring an active superuser session for privileged paths; the feature is a privileged user-toggleable path advertising access to data beyond normal pagination bounds with no legitimate reason for pagination to grant superusers different data (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a privileged, user-toggleable code path (`optimized_pagination=true`) gated by `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` (organization_auditlogs.py). It does not use any “active superuser session” helper/check (e.g., `is_active_superuser(request)`), so if the project expects that convention for privileged behaviors, this change would bypass it. However, that convention/requirement is not verifiable from the diff alone, so it’s best treated as a concrete review concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The change to BasePaginator.get_result affects every cursor-paginated endpoint in Sentry; a malformed forward cursor with a negative offset is now silently clamped to page 1 instead of surfacing an error, hiding client bugs and changing behavior for unrelated endpoints without justification (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182)

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py:get_result`, the diff changes slicing from `queryset[offset:stop]` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]` where `start_offset = max(0, offset)` for non-`prev` cursors. This means a forward cursor carrying a negative `cursor.offset` will no longer raise/propagate an error from negative queryset slicing (previous behavior), and will instead be silently coerced to `0`, effectively returning the first page. This is a global behavior change in the base paginator logic (not gated to the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`) and can hide malformed client cursors and alter pagination semantics across endpoints using this paginator.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator does not change the query at all; get_result is a near-verbatim copy of BasePaginator.get_result with the same build_queryset, slice, and count_hits path, so the claimed performance gains cannot be delivered and the duplication must be kept in sync with the base class (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820)

adjudication.rationale: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` is largely a copy of existing paginator logic (same `build_queryset`, `count_hits`/`known_hits` handling, slicing, cursor building), which creates a real maintainability/sync risk (kept in sync with base behavior). However, the finding’s claim that it “does not change the query at all” is not strictly true: it adds a conditional branch that allows negative slicing when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0` (and also tweaks offset handling via `start_offset`). So this is a valid review concern about duplication and likely overstated performance claims, but not a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator, the modified BasePaginator.get_result slice logic, or the new optimized_pagination endpoint branch; a single test with one audit-log row would have caught the datetime TypeError and negative-slice failures (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:820)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces verifiable broken behavior in the new pagination path. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key`, it does `math.floor/ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, which will raise a `TypeError` if the key is a `datetime` (the audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime` and would typically paginate on that field). Additionally, both the modified `BasePaginator.get_result` and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` can slice querysets with a negative start offset when `cursor.is_prev` or when `enable_advanced_features` is set; Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and will fail. The finding’s “no tests cover” claim isn’t provable from the diff, but the cited runtime failures are directly implied by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The added comment in src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26 claims negative offsets are now supported, but the line below is unchanged and nothing validates or handles them; the OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring's claim of backward compatibility with existing cursor implementations is also false since its cursor values are incompatible with DateTimePaginator cursors on the same endpoint

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims negative offsets are “not validated or handled,” but the diff *does* add offset handling in `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`) and in the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (explicit branch for `cursor.offset < 0` when `enable_advanced_features`). Also, `Cursor.offset = int(offset)` already permits negative integers; no additional change in `cursors.py` is required for that. The second claim about cursor incompatibility between `DateTimePaginator` and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff (we can’t see `DateTimePaginator`’s cursor encoding/format here), so stating it as fact overreaches what the diff proves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: optimized_pagination is a new public query parameter not added to the endpoint's extend_schema parameters or documented anywhere, and it bypasses the existing query-param serializer (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:67)

adjudication.rationale: In `organization_auditlogs.py`, the new behavior is gated by `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` (added around the pagination block), which reads a raw query parameter directly rather than going through the existing `self.get_filter_params(request, organization)` parsing/validation used for other query params. That makes `optimized_pagination` effectively a new public query parameter outside the endpoint’s normal query-param handling. The diff does not show any schema/`extend_schema` updates, so whether it’s documented there cannot be verified from this diff alone, but the bypass of the existing query-param serializer is directly evidenced.
